deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is from the material behind Riemann's posthumous memoir 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (ed. Hattendorff, 1867). The section treats a minimal surface bounded by two straight-line polygons in the parallel planes X=0 and X=h. η is the stereographic image of the surface normal, and H is the doubly connected region of the η-plane that the surface maps to. The previous page gives dX = -i (du/dlogη)^2 dlogη, with Y and Z also expressed by integrals. It then specialises to the symmetric case: two regular n-gons forming the top and bottom of a right frustum of a regular pyramid. In the machine transcription the letter 'q' is Riemann's η.

Step 1 (normalisation in the η-plane). The 'Umkehrpunkte' of the normal are the points where the normal turns back. In this case they sit at the midpoints of the polygon sides: points A for one polygon, A' for the other. Choose the y-axis perpendicular to one side. Then one point A and one point A' lie on the real η-axis, because the moduli η0, η1 must have a common centre (the origin). Rotational symmetry then puts all A on one circle |η|=η0 and all A' on another circle |η|=η1. These are presumably concentric circles centred at 0. On each circle the points form the vertices of a regular polygon, and each A lies on the same ray from 0 as an A'.

Step 2 (normalisation of the two-sheeted surface T). H is represented on a two-sheeted Riemann surface T over the t-plane. The branch points include t=±i; from the next page they are presumably ±i and ±i/κ. Two points of T may be prescribed, so let the first A and the first A' correspond to t=0 in the two sheets. By symmetry, the real-axis segment of the η-plane from A to A' then corresponds in T to the path that runs from t=0 up the imaginary axis to the branch point t=i and back to t=0 in the other sheet. Hence a certain function φ(t, √Δ), rational in t and the radical of T, takes purely imaginary values for purely imaginary t.

Struck-out step. Riemann first concluded directly that φ = t ψ(t^2) with ψ rational in t^2, then deleted this. Imaginarity alone does not exclude dependence on the radical.

Step 3 (the inversion symmetry). The substitution η η' = η0 η1 maps H onto itself. It interchanges the A' with the A, in reversed order. In T this is the sheet interchange: η' corresponds to the same value of t, but in the other sheet. Its fixed points are η = ±√(η0 η1), which correspond to the branch points t=±i. This is consistent with c = √(η0 η1) on the next page.

Since dlogη + dlogη' = 0, φ takes the same value at corresponding points of both sheets. My inference is that φ is a quotient such as dX/dlogη, where numerator and denominator both change sign under the symmetry. Being symmetric in the sheets, φ is single-valued on the t-sphere, i.e. rational in t. Combining this with Step 2 gives the restored conclusion φ = t ψ(t^2).

Transition. This motivates mapping T onto a surface S by s^2 = (1+t^2)/(1+κ^2 t^2), continued on the next page. There the upper half of T becomes the s-plane slit along [1, 1/κ] and [-1, -1/κ]. X becomes an elliptic integral of the first kind, X ∝ ∫ ds/√((1-s^2)(1-κ^2 s^2)).
errors: No outright error on the page. Riemann's first inference (φ purely imaginary on the imaginary axis ⇒ φ = tψ(t^2)) was unjustified as long as φ could depend on the radical of the two-sheeted surface T; he correctly crossed it out and re-derived it after proving rationality via the sheet-exchange symmetry ηη'=η0η1.

Even after rationality, 'imaginary on the imaginary axis' gives φ(-conj t) = -conj φ(t). To get oddness φ(-t) = -φ(t) one also needs real coefficients, i.e. φ real for real t. This presumably comes from the reflection symmetry in the real η-axis; it is left implicit.
The identity of φ (written φ(1,Δt) in the transcription) is not defined on this page; the reconstruction as a sheet-invariant quotient such as dX/dlogη is an inference, not explicit in the text.
(Next page, not this one:) 1-s^2 = -(1-κ^2)t^2/(1+κ^2 t^2), not κ^2(1-κ^2)t^2/(1+κ^2 t^2) as transcribed there.

results.what: Use of the symmetry of the regular-polygon frustum configuration to normalise the Gauss-map region H (branch points on concentric circles, aligned radially) and the two-sheeted surface T (t=0 at A, A'; branch point t=i on the real η-axis).
results.modern_name: Symmetry reduction / normalisation of the Weierstrass–Enneper data via the Gauss map for a doubly-connected minimal surface (Riemann's polygonal Plateau problem)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (memoir published posthumously 1867 by Hattendorff); later Schwarz, Weierstrass

results.what: The inversion ηη'=η0η1 realises the symmetry exchanging the two boundary polygons. It acts on T as the sheet interchange, so a sheet-invariant function is rational in t; combined with the imaginary-axis condition, φ = tψ(t^2).
results.modern_name: Descent of a function invariant under the hyperelliptic (sheet) involution to the quotient sphere; anticonformal reflection symmetry giving odd rational functions
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (theory of Riemann surfaces/algebraic functions, 1857; minimal surface memoir 1867)

results.what: Reduction (completed on the next page) via s^2=(1+t^2)/(1+κ^2t^2) to a doubly slit s-plane, with the height X given by an elliptic integral of the first kind.
results.modern_name: Riemann's doubly-periodic/annular minimal surfaces spanning two polygons in parallel planes (elliptic-function parametrisation)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann, Gesammelte Werke, 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (1867)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of material that appears in Riemann's posthumously published minimal-surface memoir (Hattendorff 1867), including the frustum-of-a-regular-pyramid example, the substitution s^2=(1+t^2)/(1+κ^2t^2) and the elliptic integral for X. The only extra interest is seeing the deleted, premature inference and its correction.

checkable.asserts: 1-s^2 = -(1-κ^2)t^2/(1+κ^2t^2) (should be 0); this corrects the version on the next page.
The fixed points of the inversion η -> η0η1/η are ±sqrt(η0η1), matching the branch points t=±i and c=sqrt(η0η1).
Example: an odd rational function with real coefficients, tψ(t^2), is purely imaginary on the imaginary axis (real part 0).

transcription_corrections: 'q', 'q0 q1', 'q-Fläche', 'd log q' should read η, η0 η1, η-Fläche (η-Ebene), d log η: Riemann's eta was misread as q.
'für den Abstände q0 q1 einen Mittelpunkt' should probably read 'für die Abstände η0, η1 einen Mittelpunkt'.
'auf zwei aneinanderstoßenden Kreisen' is doubtful: mathematically it should be 'auf zwei concentrischen Kreisen' (|η|=η0, |η|=η1) with the points on common radius vectors.
'φ(1,Δt)' is probably φ(t, √Δ) or similar, i.e. a function of t and the radical of the two-sheeted surface T; as written it is not meaningful.
The interlinear insertion should be read as 'der erst zwischen A u. A' liegende Theil der reellen Axe in der η-Fläche'.
'Aus der oben genannten Bemerkung' may be 'Aus der obigen Bemerkung' (wording uncertain).
